title: `EditorResourcePreview::_idle_callback` can stall the editor for longer than intended
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.8.dev [49f68a134ec7997dda2eb5b92a1f43eb37273498] - Reproducible in 4.7.1.stable ### System information Godot v4.8.dev (0d9259106) - Fedora Linux 44 (Forty Four) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Single-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (radeonsi, gfx1201, ACO, DRM 3.64, 7.1.3-201.fc44.x86_64) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 60.39 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description When launching the editor for a project that uses the Compatibility renderer, and said project has a bunch of new resources, you can find that the editor is fairly unresponsive for a little while, depending on the specs of the machine and the size of the project. This is particularly prominent in the web editor on low-spec machines like Chromebooks. When profiling, this seems to stem from `EditorResourcePreview::_idle_callback`. This method is run on the main thread when using the Compatibility renderer (i.e. when `RSG::rasterizer->can_create_resources_async()` returns `false`) and has a 100 ms time limit, specifically to allow the editor to remain somewhat responsive while the preview images are being generated. However, it doesn't consider the fact that idle callbacks are called both during idle processing and during physics processing, meaning you can end up spending this 100 ms time limit multiple times in a single engine iteration, the number of times of which is effectively governed by the `physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame` project setting, which is set to 8 by default, so up to 900-ish ms in total when including the process frame. This is made worse by the fact that spending 100 ms on anything in a single frame will more or less guarantee that multiple physics frames will be processed during the next frame, in order for the fixed physics timestep to "catch up", leading to a "spiral of death" until all the preview images have been generated. While these long stalls aren't all that noticeable on most desktop machines, lower spec machines like Chromebooks running the web editor suffers heavily, as you might see from this profiling, where each red section is a 1-second long frame: (The first screenshot shows a "zoomed out" view of the 1-second long frames, and the second a close-up of one of them.) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the MRP on a low-spec machine (e.g. a Chromebook using the web editor) 2. Wait for the editor UI to show up (i.e. past the splash screen) 3. Try interacting with the editor (e.g. just hover over stuff) 4. Note the severe latency of the interactions. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [resource-preview-stall.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30090232/resource-preview-stall.zip)
